units.text: This week, Apple is hosting its first-ever dedicated smart home event. While the company hasn’t shared details about what it will reveal at the “Welcome Home experience” in New York City on Tuesday, October 13th, it doesn’t take an army of internet sleuths to deduce we’ll get news about Apple Home — specifically, new hardware. Apple finally seems to be taking the smart home seriously.

According to Bloomberg, Apple will release a smart home display alongside a refreshed HomePod Mini and Apple TV. The display, which MacRumors reports may be called HomeView, is arguably Apple’s first dedicated Apple Home hardware since it launched the HomeKit platform in 2014. As exciting as this is (and I’ll be there in person to check it out), the real shift will be bringing Siri AI and Apple Intelligence into the home. Apple is years behind Google and Amazon in smart-home hardware, but success in the home depends far more on software. That’s where Apple could leapfrog the competition.

New home hardware is long overdue. Apple announced the HomePod Mini on October 13th, 2020, six years to the day from this week’s event, and the newest Apple TV 4K is now four years old. And those aren’t dedicated smart home devices; they’re more content-consumption gadgets with a side of home automation. The new smart display is reportedly designed to be the heart of Apple Home, marking a complete reboot of the ecosystem, and Apple Home users have wanted it for years.

[Image: Smart displays, like this Echo Show 8, can be used to view footage from home security cameras. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/LR6B5928.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]

The smart display category has a bumpy history. Amazon and Google have launched several generations of these voice- and touchscreen-controlled smart speakers that can control smart home gadgets like lights and locks, pull up doorbell camera feeds, and make video calls. But the category has seen very little innovation, and its best use case has been serving as a digital photo frame.

Based on leaks, Apple’s product doesn’t sound that different from what’s come before. According to Bloomberg, it will have a 6-inch square display on a speaker base or as a wall-mounted option, facial recognition to show your personal messages and calendar, a minimalist touchscreen interface to control locks and thermostats, and FaceTime and intercom calls. Nothing groundbreaking, except the rumored price — $350, ouch. The difference has to be in the software and the smart assistant that powers it.

Bloomberg reports the smart display will launch with a brand-new homeOS built around Siri AI. Generative AI has breathed new life into the smart home voice assistant by both making it easier to talk to and expanding its capabilities. Until now, Apple’s new Siri AI has been MIA from its HomePods and Apple TV; when you talk to those, the old Siri responds in its basic, functional way.

[Image: Apple’s smart speakers: the HomePod and HomePod Mini. Rumors indicate that only the Mini will get a refresh this week to support Siri AI. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/24397106/236507_HomePod_2_JTuohy_0002.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

Apple is the last of the big three to bring generative AI to its home assistant. Amazon and Google launched theirs last year, but Alexa Plus is only just starting to get it right, and Google’s Gemini for Home, an underpowered version of Gemini, is a confusing mess of capabilities. Now it’s Apple’s turn, and if the company can successfully merge its superpowered personal assistant on your iPhone with a superpowered assistant for your home, it may have a hit on its hands.

That’s a very big if. So far, every company has hit significant roadblocks bringing a smarter assistant to the home. Apple announced Apple Intelligence in 2024, but Siri AI only arrived last month; a version of Alexa Plus was announced in 2023 but didn’t launch until 2025; Gemini for Home is still in an early access program and split into a weird hybrid model where its more capable version, Gemini Live, is restricted from interacting with the home.

These cautious approaches are down to the fact that the home is a big, complicated, messy, multi-user environment that is hard to control. An agentic AI getting something wrong could have consequences far greater than accidentally sending an email. Smart home systems are connected to critical infrastructure like HVAC, locks, and security systems. Every home is different, with unique needs — there is no single plug-and-play solution.

Progress has been made toward solving one of the smart home’s biggest challenges: interoperability, with open standards like Matter and Thread promising to make setting up and using a smart home easier. But these are protocols, not software. It’s the platforms that have to make the smart home work. Here is where Apple may have the edge.

Four years ago, after helping found Matter, Apple rebuilt HomeKit’s underlying architecture and revamped the Home app, laying a strong foundation. That move also let Apple Home work with more devices from more manufacturers (previously, it was limited to those willing to go through the often arduous HomeKit approval process).
[Image: The Apple Home app works across Apple devices. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/hero_homepod_lockup__d8j0cm45ask2_large.webp?quality=90&strip=all]

However, a smart home isn’t just about the devices you put in it. It’s about making them work together. That’s where Siri AI and Apple Intelligence could play a major role. While Apple used Gemini models to build Siri AI, Google itself has struggled to deliver a compelling experience in the home. So Apple’s opportunity lies in execution. Its more curated approach to third-party hardware has held it back, but it also means Apple arrives at this crucial moment with less technical debt and a cleaner foundation for building an AI-powered smart home.

This will be the next level for the smart home; with reliable data and context, your home could know who’s in it, where they are, and what they need, and, combined with knowing the status of every device, become proactive. For example, it could alert you that the oven is on and no one is home, suggest turning off the AC when a window is left open, and route messages and notifications to the room you’re in.

This is still a distant promise, however. Today, Apple Home has significant limitations: it doesn’t support every type of home device (no fridges, washing machines, or EV chargers); it can’t control every feature of many device types; and its automations are limited compared to the competition (notably lacking conditional programming options inside the app). All this makes the Home app very easy to use, but extremely underpowered.

With Siri AI, Apple could unlock many of those capabilities via voice instead of building complicated menu interfaces. You could just tell Siri what you want your smart home to do. Alexa Plus offers this with the ability to create routines using your voice; Gemini for Home lets you use natural language in its Home app chatbot to set up automations; and many smart home companies are adopting AI in their apps to cut through UI complexity and make devices and features easier to use.

A big question remains: do people really want a smart home? Many of us have spent years frustrated with systems that hold so much promise but routinely fail to deliver, leaving us spending weekends troubleshooting why the garage door won’t open. The truly dedicated have turned to Home Assistant, a powerful platform that can do almost anything you want, if you’re willing to do the work. But for most people, beyond a few solutions to specific problems, the smart home just isn’t worth it.

To win in the smart home and bring the category mainstream, Apple needs more than just great hardware; it needs a superior software experience that makes the smart home easy to use. It needs to integrate seamlessly with third-party devices and deliver a consistent, reliable experience, relying on local control wherever possible and making sure products just work.

Apple is reportedly partnering with LG and others to develop products for an “Apple Home Collection” that will add a layer of Apple polish to the smart home experience. While this might sound like going back to the walled garden of the HomeKit days, Matter ensures interoperability with other platforms. Apple can’t make everything for the smart home, but it can make sure that everything works with its platform.

Most crucially, Apple will need to double down on its commitment to privacy and data security, especially as it opens the home to Apple Intelligence’s cloud-based capabilities. If Apple can deliver on all of this, its highly anticipated smart home display might justify its price. But the real test will be whether Siri can make the smart home live up to its promise.

evidence.title: The iPhone Duo’s cooling system hides a clever trick inside its hinge - 9to5Mac

units.text: While a folding iPhone posed a new challenge for Apple’s thermal engineering team, they came up with a creative way to leverage the device’s hinge to their advantage. Here are the details.
iPhone Duo’s hinge features a flexible graphite pipe

PCMag recently sat down with Dan Murray, Apple’s vice president of silicon engineering, and Banafsheh Barabadi, the company’s senior manager of thermal product design, to discuss the architecture of the A20 Pro chip.

The new SoC, which powers the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo, is Apple’s first iPhone chip built on a 2 nm process, following the technology’s debut with the M6 chip in the Mac mini in August.

And while the A20 Pro was designed with all three new iPhones in mind, the iPhone Duo version packs some additional capabilities. These include a second display engine to run both screens simultaneously.
From PCMag:

The iPhone Duo’s A20 Pro variant is just slightly different. “For iPhone Duo, we added a second display engine to support simultaneous operation of the inner and outer displays,” says Murray, “and with the increased CPU and GPU performance, we ensure we can deliver a smooth user experience across the displays. For the inner display, we also added support for placing the FaceTime camera behind the display.”

The report offers a really interesting, in-depth look at the A20 Pro’s thermals and the new vapor chamber Apple developed to keep them at bay. That includes what Apple calls “metal over foam,” a material that iFixit also examined during its recent teardown of the iPhone 18 Pro.

The second pillar is a new material that bridges the gap between the A20 Pro and the vapor chamber. “We call it metal over foam,” says Barabadi, and it “basically creates a direct thermal and mechanically compliant coupling between the SoC and the vapor chamber. It is highly effective in removing the heat, meeting the strict mechanical requirements of the system. It took us months of development to get the material properties exactly right to be able to use this material.”

Perhaps the most interesting tidbit from the story is what Apple did to improve the iPhone Duo’s thermal performance, particularly given the challenges of dissipating heat in a device that doubles in thickness when folded.
From the report:

“This was one of the most technically challenging aspects of our design,” says Barabadi. To surmount the issue, Apple routed a flexible graphite pipe through the hinge itself to transfer heat between the two halves, thereby increasing the surface area available for heat dissipation. “This part need[ed] to be co-engineered between our thermal team and the mechanical team. It’s a flexible material that needs to survive, as you can imagine, many hinge cycles while maintaining its thermal connectivity, and also its structural integrity throughout the product life cycle.”

PCMag’s interview with Murray and Barabadi also goes into the A20 Pro’s architecture, including the benefits of placing the DRAM next to the processor rather than stacking it on top, and you can read it in full here.

evidence.discovery_lead: IT之家 10 月 13 日消息，科技媒体 PCMag 昨日（10 月 12 日）发布博文，采访了苹果公司两位高管， 首次披露了苹果首款折叠屏手机 iPhone Duo 的铰链散热方案。 苹果公司芯片工程副总裁丹 · 默里（Dan Murray）和苹果散热产品设计高级经理巴纳夫什 · 巴拉巴迪（Banafsheh Barabadi）在接受该媒体采访时，详细披露了苹果的散热定制方案， 从而在 iPhone 18 Pro、iPhone 18 Pro、iPhone Duo 中最大限度提升 A20 Pro 芯片持续性能输出。 在 A20 Pro 封装方面，该芯片采用晶圆级多芯片模块（WMCM）封装，将 DRAM 从处理器上方移至旁边。IT之家援引博文介绍，苹果称这一设计为芯片到均热板建立直接热通路，消除了此前封装叠层（POP）方案中的散热瓶颈。 iPhone 18 Pro 后盖内部视图 在 iPhone 18 Pro 和 Pro Max 中， 均热板表面积为 iPhone 17 Pro 的 3 倍 ，内部含有更多去离子水。该均热板同时承担机械骨架功能，电池和逻辑板直接安装其上，并使用 80% 再生不锈钢。 iPhone 18 Pro 内部视图，显示屏侧面 苹果还在屏幕背面采用纳米孪晶铜金属板，并叠加高导热石墨层。两种材料共同改善显示屏横向散热，减少热点，同时满足显示屏所需的机械强度。 iPhone 18 Pro 的 VC 均热板和电池 iPhone 18 Pro 石墨层 iPhone Duo 采用较 iPhone 18 Pro 更薄的均热板，且悬浮于机身中部，由于折叠后机身厚度增加一倍，苹果通过铰链内的柔性石墨管连接两侧散热结构。 柔性石墨管是一种由石墨材料构成的柔性导热部件，可在有限空间内弯曲布置。它将热量从发热区域传导至其他区域，常用于手机、笔记本等内部空间紧凑的电子设备散热。 iPhone Duo 内部视图 苹果表示，新散热系统支持游戏、视频录制和设备端 AI 等负载，iPhone 18 Pro 的持续 GPU 性能较 iPhone 17 Pro 提升 35%；A20 Pro 的 CPU 性能提升 20%，图形性能提升 40%。 苹果高管详解 A20 Pro 散热定制方案：WMCM 封装将 DRAM 移至处理器旁，iPhone 18 Pro 均热板面积达上代 3 倍，折叠屏 Duo 更在铰链内藏柔性石墨管连接两侧散热。GPU 持续性能提升 35%，图形性能提升 40%。#苹果折叠屏iPhone#

units.text: IT之家 10 月 13 日消息，科技媒体 PCMag 昨日（10 月 12 日）发布博文，采访了苹果公司两位高管，首次披露了苹果首款折叠屏手机 iPhone Duo 的铰链散热方案。
苹果公司芯片工程副总裁丹 · 默里（Dan Murray）和苹果散热产品设计高级经理巴纳夫什 · 巴拉巴迪（Banafsheh Barabadi）在接受该媒体采访时，详细披露了苹果的散热定制方案，从而在 iPhone 18 Pro、iPhone 18 Pro、iPhone Duo 中最大限度提升 A20 Pro 芯片持续性能输出。
在 A20 Pro 封装方面，该芯片采用晶圆级多芯片模块（WMCM）封装，将 DRAM 从处理器上方移至旁边。IT之家援引博文介绍，苹果称这一设计为芯片到均热板建立直接热通路，消除了此前封装叠层（POP）方案中的散热瓶颈。
iPhone 18 Pro 后盖内部视图
在 iPhone 18 Pro 和 Pro Max 中，均热板表面积为 iPhone 17 Pro 的 3 倍，内部含有更多去离子水。该均热板同时承担机械骨架功能，电池和逻辑板直接安装其上，并使用 80% 再生不锈钢。
iPhone 18 Pro 内部视图，显示屏侧面
苹果还在屏幕背面采用纳米孪晶铜金属板，并叠加高导热石墨层。两种材料共同改善显示屏横向散热，减少热点，同时满足显示屏所需的机械强度。
iPhone 18 Pro 的 VC 均热板和电池
iPhone 18 Pro 石墨层
iPhone Duo 采用较 iPhone 18 Pro 更薄的均热板，且悬浮于机身中部，由于折叠后机身厚度增加一倍，苹果通过铰链内的柔性石墨管连接两侧散热结构。
柔性石墨管是一种由石墨材料构成的柔性导热部件，可在有限空间内弯曲布置。它将热量从发热区域传导至其他区域，常用于手机、笔记本等内部空间紧凑的电子设备散热。
iPhone Duo 内部视图
苹果表示，新散热系统支持游戏、视频录制和设备端 AI 等负载，iPhone 18 Pro 的持续 GPU 性能较 iPhone 17 Pro 提升 35%；A20 Pro 的 CPU 性能提升 20%，图形性能提升 40%。

evidence.discovery_lead: 快科技10月13日消息，据Gartner数据， 今年第三季度全球PC出货量降至5540万台，同比下降22.4%，为2023年初以来最低水平。此前IDC公布的同期数据也显示，全球PC出货量同比下滑20.1%。 Gartner研究负责人表示， 第三季度出货量下降，是产品价格上涨、制造商调整有限零部件分配优先级，以及市场向高价位、高配置产品转移等多重因素共同作用的结果。 数据显示，今年第二季度DRAM供应价格同比上涨至原来的5倍。随着PC制造商将增加的成本转嫁至终端售价，消费者购买和更换设备的支出明显增加，进而导致第三季度PC出货量大幅减少。 同时，主要厂商削减低价产品供应，进一步抬高了消费者换机门槛；企业客户则将更多预算投向工作站、AI PC等产品。 从厂商表现看， 全球前六大PC制造商第三季度出货量均同比下降。其中，惠普降幅最大，达30.9%；苹果降幅最小，为7.1%。受主要MacBook产品线支撑，苹果市场份额同比提高1.7个百分点。 作为对比，2023年第一季度全球PC出货量为5520万台，较2022年同期下降30%，当时市场下滑主要与大型PC制造商库存过剩有关。 此次出货量再度接近该低点，主要影响因素已转向存储器价格上涨、产品结构调整以及企业采购方向变化。

units.text: 苹果与Epic Games在一份10月9日提交的联合状态报告中，就苹果应向Epic提供哪些内部文件、何时完成披露出现分歧。Epic指控苹果拖延提交法院要求的材料，并请求法官命令其最迟于11月1日完成；苹果则称自己没有拖延，已同意Epic提出的16项文件请求、27名资料保管人及其搜索词，只是相关搜查范围庞大，无法在Epic要求的期限内全部完成。文件是双方分别陈述立场的联合报告，并非法院对争议作出的裁定。

争议源于美国加州北区联邦地区法院5月20日的命令。苹果须提交与其外链购买佣金方案决策过程有关的非特权文件，首轮文件原定8月24日前交付。Epic在报告中称，截至提交文件时，苹果针对这一决策过程仅提供55份回应文件，其中16份有中度至大量删节，4份为重复或近似重复；苹果另称仅有15份文件因特权而未披露。Epic认为这些材料没有展示苹果业务人员如何确定佣金率，并称8月24日提交的34份文件大多是日历邀请、诉讼材料和删节文件。
双方对已提交资料的意义也意见相反。苹果称，8月13日已经交付逾1800份文件及大量交易、账单数据，包括覆盖美国App Store数十亿笔交易的数据；这些数据涉及约210万个应用，并为其专家分析和佣金提案提供了输入。Epic则认为，这些数据和专家报告材料并未说明苹果内部人员究竟如何选择新费率，也未提供相关讨论、商业分析或决策记录。

Epic还要求披露更多参与者的文件，并将搜索范围扩展到美国以外的外链佣金方案，认为苹果在其他地区的经验可能影响美国费率。苹果反驳称，其提案是在法院和第九巡回上诉法院指导下制定的，决策过程比此前推出外链购买机制时窄得多，主要由少数高管在数月内通过有限会议作出；为避免程序陷入进一步争论，苹果已接受Epic提出的27名资料保管人和搜索词，但保留必要时调整的权利。苹果表示，对海外佣金资料可不设地域限制地检索四名核心决策者的文件，但不认为有必要对所有27人开展全球范围搜索。
披露时限方面，苹果称预计11月1日前后能实质完成7名资料保管人的文件交付，其他人员的资料则预计在11月25日前后实质完成；苹果没有承诺届时一定全部交齐。Epic要求法院要求苹果立即分批交付，并在11月1日前完成全部相关材料。双方还同意，Epic在5月命令下的60天回应期限尚未开始计算，因为文件披露范围仍在协商。法官尚未就Epic的期限请求或双方的范围争议作出裁定。
这轮证据开示围绕苹果拟议的App Store外链佣金展开。此前苹果因如何执行允许应用引导用户到外部支付的禁令，被地区法院认定藐视法庭；苹果已就该认定向美国最高法院上诉。最高法院今年6月同意审理其中一个问题，但地区法院仍继续处理外链佣金方案及其事实材料。

units.text: IT之家 10 月 13 日消息，科技媒体 LTT Labs 实测显示，在苹果 iPhone 18 Pro 和 iPhone 18 Pro Max 上，使用未支持可变电压供电（AVS）的 USB PD 充电器，也能达到媲美支持 AVS 充电器接近的快充速度。
AVS 是一种 USB Power Delivery 充电协议功能，支持充电器根据被充电设备的请求，在较宽范围内精细调整输出电压。USB PD 是 USB Power Delivery 的缩写，是基于 USB-C 接口的快充供电标准。设备与充电器通过通信协商电压和电流，从而在安全范围内提高充电功率。
IT之家附上官方声明内容如下：
iPhone 18 Pro 只需约 15 分钟即可充至最高 50% 电量，使用无线充电时可在 30 分钟内充至最高 50% 电量。iPhone 18 Pro Max 仅需有线充电 5 分钟即可提供约 7 小时视频播放时间。
Apple 于 2026 年 7 月使用试生产的 iPhone 18 Pro 和 iPhone 18 Pro Max 机型和软件，搭配 USB-C 充电线和型号为 A3351 的 Apple 40W 动态电源适配器 (最高 60W) 进行了此项测试。
有线快速充电需使用支持 60 瓦功率的 USB-C 充电线与支持可调电压供电 (AVS) 的 USB PD 3.1 (或更高版本) 电源适配器。快速充电测试采用放电完全的各款 iPhone 机型。时间从设备启动时显示 Apple 标志开始测算。
充电时间依电源适配器、设置、使用情况和环境因素可能有所差异；实际结果可能有所不同。60 瓦或更大功率的电源适配器（另行出售）须搭配 USB-C 充电线使用；35 瓦或更大功率的电源适配器须搭配 MagSafe 充电器使用（均另行出售）。
LTT Labs 对比使用支持 AVS 的 Apple 40W 动态电源适配器，与不支持 AVS 的 UGREEN Nexode 140W 充电器，并记录输出功率与充满电所需时间。
在 iPhone 18 Pro 上，两款充电器的输出功率变化几乎一致，充满电所需时间也相同。该机构据此判断，AVS 并非该机型达到高速充电的必要条件。
iPhone 18 Pro Max 的测试结果出现较小差距。使用 Apple 适配器时，充电初期输出约 50W，耗时 82 分钟充满；使用 UGREEN 充电器时，输出未达到 50W，耗时 84 分钟充满。
LTT Labs 结论指出，只要 USB PD 充电器具备约 40W 至 50W 输出，即使不支持 AVS，iPhone 18 Pro 系列的快充速度也与 AVS 充电器基本相同。

evidence.discovery_lead: IT之家 10 月 13 日消息，科技媒体 DPReview 今天（10 月 13 日）发布博文，报道称在苹果 iPhone 18 Pro 和 iPhone 18 Pro Max 上， 用户手动设置快门速度后会停止多帧堆叠，仅拍摄单帧照片，夜间模式也会失效。 该媒体测试指出，iPhone 18 Pro 和 iPhone 18 Pro Max 上通过 Pro 级控制选项（Pro Controls），手动设置快门速度后，会停止多帧堆叠（frame stacking）。 iPhone 18 Pro 系列于 9 月发布，主摄像头首次配备机械可变光圈，并新增手动设置光圈、快门速度和白平衡的 Pro 控制功能。该媒体称在苹果官方宣传中，并未提及手动快门速度与计算摄影处理之间的取舍。 该媒体测试显示，全自动模式和手动光圈模式均保留多帧堆叠。手机会连续拍摄多帧，对齐并合并为一张照片，从而降低噪点、提升动态范围。但在任何包含手动快门速度的设置场景下，iPhone 18 Pro 系列均改为单帧拍摄。 DPReview 在三脚架上使用主摄像头拍摄静态场景，覆盖日光至夜间环境，并分别测试全自动、手动光圈、手动快门速度及两者均手动设置四种模式。 结果显示，光线充足时，手动快门与自动曝光的差异较小。在弱光或深阴影场景中，手动快门照片的噪点更明显。在夜间样张中，f/1.48、1/15 秒、ISO 10000、夜间模式关闭条件下，手动快门与自动曝光的差异清晰可见。 自动曝光 手动快门 参考 IT之家附上原帖地址，点此可以前往浏览更多拍摄样张 科技媒体 DPReview 今天（10 月 13 日）发布博文，报道称在苹果 iPhone 18 Pro 和 iPhone 18 Pro Max 上，用户手动设置快门速度后会停止多帧堆叠，仅拍摄单帧照片，夜间模式也会失效。

evidence.title: 爱回收买iPad靠谱吗：iPad Air M2到手验机全记录

units.text: 最近想买一台 iPad 用来做笔记和看视频，在 iPad Air M2 和 iPad Pro 之间选了前者 —— 性价比更高。全新要 4000 多，我在爱回收严选找到一台 3000 出头的，成色标注 95 新。今天把我从下单到验机的全过程分享出来，聊聊爱回收买 iPad 靠谱吗。
iPad 品类要注意什么
买二手 iPad 有两个容易忽略的点：一是屏幕坏点和暗斑，iPad 屏幕大，坏点更难发现，而且如果在看视频时碰到暗斑会很影响体验；二是 Apple Pencil 配对兼容性，不同代 iPad 支持不同型号的 Apple Pencil，买之前要确认清楚。爱回收严选的 iPad 有 6 档成色分级（不同于手机的 7 档），商品页标注了屏幕状态和 Apple Pencil 兼容信息。
我为什么选了教育优惠之外的二手
很多人买 iPad 会走教育优惠，确实能便宜几百块。但教育优惠的前提是你有教育资格，而且配置和存储是固定的。我在爱回收严选能找到更高配置的二手机器，价格反而比教育优惠买低配新机还便宜。当然，教育优惠买全新有完整的苹果保修，这是一个取舍。
我收到 iPad Air M2 后的验机流程
到货后我花了 40 分钟做了一套全面验机：
屏幕检查：纯白、纯黑、纯红 / 绿 / 蓝背景下检查坏点和暗斑
触控测试：全区域触控响应测试，拖动图标到各个位置
Apple Pencil 配对：与我的 Apple Pencil Pro 配对，确认书写和压感正常
电池健康度：查看电池最大容量，较高水平
摄像头测试：前后摄像头各拍几张，成像清晰
扬声器测试：四扬声器播放音乐，确认无杂音
账号确认：无 Apple ID 绑定，激活锁已解除
外观核对：机身成色与实拍图一致，边框无严重磕碰
跨渠道对比
对比维度爱回收严选苹果教育优惠闲鱼个人卖家价格约 3000~3500 约 3800 起 3500 左右成色 95 新有质检全新不确定保修 1 年联保苹果 1 年保修无退货 7 天无理由 14 天无理由基本不退 Apple Pencil 兼容信息标注全新配件不确定朋友问过我的一些问题
Q：iPad 能配 Apple Pencil 吗？
A：iPad Air M2 支持 Apple Pencil Pro 和 Apple Pencil USB 版。买二手时确认商品页标注了兼容的 Pencil 型号，到手后实际配对测试一下。
Q：屏幕有坏点能退吗？
A：可以走 7 天无理由退货。建议到手后在纯色背景下仔细检查，有问题及时申请。
Q：教育优惠和二手哪个划算？
A：如果你有教育资格并且想買全新机，教育优惠是好选择。如果追求更高配置或更低价格，二手严选可以考虑。我的情况是需要 256G 版本，教育优惠的价格就不如二手划算了。
我的结论
爱回收买 iPad 靠谱吗？我的体会是：靠谱。爱回收严选的质检报告和 360 度实拍让我能提前了解屏幕状态。6 档成色分级也比较清晰，加上 7 天无理由退货和 1 年联保，整体购物体验比较安心。

Gartner 数据：2026Q3 全球 PC 出货量降至 2023 年初以来最低水平

2026/10/12 16:40:44 来源：IT之家 作者：溯波（实习） 责编：溯波
评论：

IT之家 10 月 12 日消息，Gartner（高德纳）当地时间今日发布初步数据，认为全球个人电脑出货量仅有 5,540 万台，同比下滑 22.4%，是 2023Q1 以来的最低水平。

Gartner 首席研究员 Namrata Banerjee 表示，存储半导体成本上升的影响现在已经完全反映在 PC 价格上；PC 市场正在经历一波高端化浪潮，消费者更难负担换机成本。

主要市场参与者中，联想维持市占第一，苹果、华硕、宏碁的表现好于行业平均，惠普、戴尔的出货减少相对更为严重。
